sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Last spring, the mayor of New York City, Eric Adams, held a press conference at a construction site in lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 去年春天，纽约市市长埃里克·亚当斯在曼哈顿下城的一个建筑工地举行了新闻发布会。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: He was there to promote a major pillar in his housing plan.
sentences.zh: 他到那里是为了推广他住房计划中的一个重要支柱。

sentences.en: We must be a city of yes.
sentences.zh: 我们必须成为一个“应允之城”。

sentences.en: We have to think differently and we have to lean into how do we have a different approach to housing.
sentences.zh: 我们必须换个角度思考，必须倾力探索如何采取不同的住房方针。

sentences.en: Adams was wearing a hard hat and a windbreaker that said Mayor Eric Adams on it.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯戴着安全帽，穿着一件印有“埃里克·亚当斯市长”字样的防风夹克。

sentences.en: And he wasn't speaking at any regular old construction site.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不是在随便哪个普通的建筑工地讲话。

sentences.en: That's producer Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人克里斯·贝鲁比。

sentences.en: Mayor Adams was giving his speech in a former office tower.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯市长是在一栋前办公大楼里发表讲话的。

sentences.en: A few years ago, this building was filled with cubicles and polymer desks and copy machines and most importantly, thousands of white collar workers.
sentences.zh: 几年前，这栋楼里还挤满了隔间、聚合物办公桌、复印机，最重要的是，还有成千上万的白领员工。

sentences.en: But during the pandemic, the workers stopped coming in.
sentences.zh: 但在疫情期间，员工们不再来了。

sentences.en: And this 24-story building sat largely empty.
sentences.zh: 于是这栋24层的大楼大部分时间都空置着。

sentences.en: So today, the building is being renovated.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，这栋楼正在进行翻新。

sentences.en: And by next summer, it's going to be filled with over 500 new apartments.
sentences.zh: 到明年夏天，它将容纳500多套新公寓。

sentences.en: Right now in Manhattan, 18% of office space is vacant.
sentences.zh: 目前在曼哈顿，18%的办公空间处于闲置状态。

sentences.en: At the same time, the city of New York has a major housing problem with more than 100,000 people using the municipal shelter system.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，纽约市面临严重的住房问题，有超过10万人使用市政收容系统。

sentences.en: So Eric Adams and city officials are talking a lot about taking those empty offices and filling them up with people.
sentences.zh: 因此，埃里克·亚当斯和市政府官员正在大力讨论如何利用这些空置办公室来安置民众。

sentences.en: The bottom line is we must make it easier to convert office buildings like the one we just toured into housing for New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 底线是，我们必须让像我们刚才参观的这类办公楼更容易改造成纽约人的住房。

sentences.en: It makes it clear what we can do with more of our vacant office building.
sentences.zh: 这明确了我们可以如何利用更多空置的办公楼。

sentences.en: You know, we're talking about millions of square feet of office space.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们谈论的是数百万平方英尺的办公空间。

sentences.en: The Adams administration actually launched a task force to look into this idea on a big scale.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯政府实际上成立了一个特别工作组，旨在从大规模层面研究这个想法。

sentences.en: Leading the task force is Dan Garodnik.
sentences.zh: 领导该工作组的是丹·加罗德尼克。

sentences.en: He's the director of New York's Department of City Planning, and he's excited about the concept.
sentences.zh: 他是纽约市城市规划局局长，他对这个概念感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Everybody knows, you know, either it's themselves or their friends or family who are working differently than they did before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道，无论是他们自己还是身边的亲友，工作方式都与疫情前不同了。

sentences.en: Everybody knows somebody who's paying way too much for rent, can't find a suitable apartment for them or their family.
sentences.zh: 每个人都认识一些人，他们支付着过高的房租，却无法为自己或家人找到合适的公寓。

sentences.en: Using those office buildings as a way to take a dent out of that problem, it makes a whole lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 利用这些办公楼来缓解这一问题，非常有意义。

sentences.en: New York is not the only big city where this is happening.
sentences.zh: 纽约并不是唯一一个出现这种情况的大城市。

sentences.en: There's talk of office to housing conversions in Chicago and L.A.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥和洛杉矶也有关于办公楼改建住房的讨论。

sentences.en: and Philadelphia and Atlanta and Toronto and actually pretty much every big city in North America.
sentences.zh: 还有费城、亚特兰大、多伦多，实际上北美几乎每个大城市都在讨论。

sentences.en: Office to housing conversions are a hot idea right now.
sentences.zh: 办公楼改建住房目前是一个热门话题。

sentences.en: They've always been a favorite hobby horse for urbanists.
sentences.zh: 这一直是城市规划者们钟爱的议题。

sentences.en: But after the pandemic, the idea hit the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 但在疫情之后，这个想法进入了主流视野。

sentences.en: And hearing about it, I have to admit, I got pretty excited because things, they are not good right now.
sentences.zh: 听到这个消息时，我必须承认，我感到非常兴奋，因为现在的状况确实不太好。

sentences.en: In most big cities, there's a housing crisis, and empty office buildings are creating a different crisis, known to urbanists as a doom loop.
sentences.zh: 在大多数大城市，住房危机普遍存在，而空置的办公楼正在制造另一种危机，城市规划者称之为“厄运循环”。

sentences.en: That's when empty office towers have this domino effect that lead to lower property taxes, which hurt city services, and they kill life downtown, which affects other businesses.
sentences.zh: 这就是当空置的办公大楼产生多米诺骨牌效应，导致房产税下降，进而损害城市服务，并扼杀市中心活力，从而影响其他企业的情况。

sentences.en: It sounds bad.
sentences.zh: 听起来很糟糕。

sentences.en: Doom loop!
sentences.zh: 厄运循环！

sentences.en: Converting an office into housing, well, it solves all these problems using one piece of property.
sentences.zh: 将办公室改造成住房，嗯，这用同一处房产解决了所有这些问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this solution just seems so obvious, so elegant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个解决方案看起来如此显而易见，如此优雅。

sentences.en: But for all the hype around this idea, I discovered there are surprisingly few projects actually underway.
sentences.zh: 但尽管这个想法被大肆宣传，我发现实际上正在进行的项目却少得惊人。

sentences.en: And many developers just don't want to get involved.
sentences.zh: 许多开发商根本不想参与其中。

sentences.en: I had to find out.
sentences.zh: 我必须找出原因。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Architects, urban planners, and superfans of office conversions talk a lot about adaptive reuse.
sentences.zh: 建筑师、城市规划者和办公楼改建的超级粉丝们经常谈论“适应性再利用”。

sentences.en: That's when you take a building and use it for something different from its original purpose.
sentences.zh: 那就是当你拿一栋建筑，将其用于与其最初目的不同的用途时。

sentences.en: Proponents of adaptive reuse love to cite Stuart Brand and his book and BBC miniseries, How Buildings Learn.
sentences.zh: 适应性再利用的支持者喜欢引用斯图尔特·布兰德及其著作和BBC迷你剧《建筑如何学习》。

sentences.en: What I'm really interested in is not architecture.
sentences.zh: 我真正感兴趣的不是建筑学。

sentences.en: It's buildings.
sentences.zh: 而是建筑本身。

sentences.en: The problem with architecture is that it's allergic to time.
sentences.zh: 建筑学的问题在于它对时间过敏。

sentences.en: Because architects keep being asked to create lasting monuments, frozen in time.
sentences.zh: 因为建筑师总是被要求创造持久的纪念碑，将其冻结在时间里。

sentences.en: But buildings have no such presumption.
sentences.zh: 但建筑并没有这种预设。

sentences.en: Buildings live in time, the same way we do.
sentences.zh: 建筑和我们一样，生活在时间之中。

sentences.en: One of Brand's big ideas is that all buildings are predictions for what the future will be like.
sentences.zh: 布兰德的一个重要观点是，所有建筑都是对未来样子的预测。

sentences.en: And those predictions are usually wrong.
sentences.zh: 而这些预测通常是错误的。

sentences.en: The basic functions and uses of most buildings change in pretty radical ways over their lifespans.
sentences.zh: 大多数建筑的基本功能和用途在其生命周期内会发生相当剧烈的变化。

sentences.en: A learning building is one that keeps being improved and refined until it reaches an adapted state.
sentences.zh: 一个“学习型建筑”是指那些不断被改进和完善，直到达到适应状态的建筑。

sentences.en: But an adapted state is not an end state.
sentences.zh: 但适应状态并非终点。

sentences.en: Even the best of buildings has to be refreshed and challenged from time to time or it becomes a beautiful corpse.
sentences.zh: 即使是最好的建筑，也必须不时地进行翻新和挑战，否则它就会变成一具美丽的尸体。

sentences.en: Big cities have a lot of these beautiful corpses at the moment.
sentences.zh: 目前大城市里有很多这样的“美丽尸体”。

sentences.en: And fans of adaptive reuse want these buildings to become housing.
sentences.zh: 而适应性再利用的拥护者希望这些建筑能变成住房。

sentences.en: And that's because the greenest building is one that's already built.
sentences.zh: 这是因为最环保的建筑就是已经建好的那栋。

sentences.en: And for this kind of office reuse, you have the potential to create new housing without riling up the people who already live close by.
sentences.zh: 对于这种办公楼再利用，你有潜力在不激怒周边居民的情况下创造新的住房。

sentences.en: It's appealing too because, you know, if we were to convert a lot of downtown offices in particular into housing,
sentences.zh: 它之所以吸引人，是因为，你知道，如果我们特别将市中心的大量办公室改造成住房，

sentences.en: that doesn't raise a lot of the concerns around gentrification and neighborhood opposition that you would get from building new housing.
sentences.zh: 这不会引发你在新建住房时通常会遇到的关于绅士化和邻里反对的许多担忧。

sentences.en: Emily Badger is a reporter for The Upshot at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 艾米丽·巴杰是《纽约时报》“Upshot”栏目的记者。

sentences.en: And fundamentally, at the end of the day, you know,
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，归根结底，你知道，

sentences.en: we're really not sort of changing the fundamental nature of how a property or a block or a neighborhood looks to people who are walking by.
sentences.zh: 对于路人来说，我们并没有真正改变房产、街区或社区的基本外观。

sentences.en: You're just sort of changing the activity that's happening inside of the building.
sentences.zh: 你只是改变了建筑内部发生的活动。

sentences.en: New development without riling up neighborhood opposition?
sentences.zh: 在不引发邻里反对的情况下进行新开发？

sentences.en: I mean, that sounds great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: So is it really possible the future of housing has been right there this whole time, towering between a parking lot and a sweet green?
sentences.zh: 那么，住房的未来一直就在那里，矗立在停车场和Sweetgreen餐厅之间，这真的可能吗？

sentences.en: I wanted to find out and to see an office to residential conversion up close.
sentences.zh: 我想一探究竟，近距离观察一次办公楼到住宅的改造。

sentences.en: I actually got to visit the same building in New York's financial district where Eric Adams did his press conference.
sentences.zh: 我实际上参观了埃里克·亚当斯举行新闻发布会的那栋位于纽约金融区的建筑。

sentences.en: It's a construction site on Water Street in lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 那是曼哈顿下城沃特街的一个建筑工地。

sentences.en: And from the street, you can see the facade changing.
sentences.zh: 从街道上看，你可以看到外立面正在发生变化。

sentences.en: The old curtain glass on the outside is being replaced by these big windows separated by light gray sills.
sentences.zh: 外面的旧幕墙玻璃正在被这些由浅灰色窗台隔开的大窗户所取代。

sentences.en: Getting there, I realized pretty quickly an active construction site is maybe not the best place for a podcast interview.
sentences.zh: 到达那里后，我很快意识到，活跃的建筑工地可能不是进行播客采访的最佳地点。

sentences.en: I also discovered I'm afraid of open-walled elevators.
sentences.zh: 我还发现我害怕开放式的施工电梯。

sentences.en: Oh, and I had no idea how to fasten the hard hat.
sentences.zh: 哦，我根本不知道怎么系好安全帽。

sentences.en: This is embarrassing, but what do I have to do with the hat to get it to sort of stick?
sentences.zh: 这很尴尬，但我该怎么做才能让帽子固定住？

sentences.en: Am I doing okay?
sentences.zh: 我做得对吗？

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: It's too tight or too loose?
sentences.zh: 是太紧了还是太松了？

sentences.en: It's a little loose, it feels like.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点松。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: After establishing my obvious experience on construction sites and my total comfort with the situation,
sentences.zh: 在展示了我对建筑工地的“丰富经验”以及对这种情况的“完全适应”之后，

sentences.en: I sat down with two of the people leading the Water Street conversion effort.
sentences.zh: 我与负责沃特街改造工作的两位负责人坐了下来。

sentences.en: They're actually part of the same team who owns the building back when it was an office tower.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是该建筑在作为办公楼时所属的同一团队的成员。

sentences.en: The two anchor tenants were insurance and health and medical companies.
sentences.zh: 那里的两个主要租户是保险公司和医疗健康公司。

sentences.en: So it was, you know, 2,000 to 3,000 people coming in daily.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，每天有2000到3000人进出。

sentences.en: This is Malik Hajar.
sentences.zh: 这位是马利克·哈贾尔。

sentences.en: Malik is the project manager for this building.
sentences.zh: 马利克是这栋楼的项目经理。

sentences.en: And before that, he was the property manager when it was still an office.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，当它还是办公楼时，他是物业经理。

sentences.en: These older, you know, 1980s, 90s cubicles and with the corner offices and the carpet and the fluorescent lighting.
sentences.zh: 这些老式的、你知道的，80、90年代的隔间，还有转角办公室、地毯和荧光灯。

sentences.en: And it is just, it's hard to even picture that this was even here before.
sentences.zh: 真的很难想象这里以前竟然是这样。

sentences.en: Malik says he misses the old office tenants, but he's excited for the new apartments to open up.
sentences.zh: 马利克说他怀念以前的办公租户，但他对新公寓的开放感到兴奋。

sentences.en: He's actually planning to live here after the construction is finished.
sentences.zh: 他实际上计划在施工完成后住在这里。

sentences.en: I will live here.
sentences.zh: 我会住在这里。

sentences.en: You're going to live here?
sentences.zh: 你要住在这里？

sentences.en: I've been here for six years.
sentences.zh: 我已经在这里待了六年了。

sentences.en: I got to, I got to see it through when it's done.
sentences.zh: 我得亲眼看着它完工。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You got to stand by your product.
sentences.zh: 你得对自己的产品负责。

sentences.en: Malik and his colleague, Joey Shillelly, work for a development company called the Van Barton Group.
sentences.zh: 马利克和他的同事乔伊·希利为一家名为Van Barton Group的开发公司工作。

sentences.en: They also developed the property next door, which used to be offices and now it's residential.
sentences.zh: 他们还开发了隔壁的房产，那里以前是办公室，现在是住宅。

sentences.en: And they're hoping to do lots of conversions like this in the future.
sentences.zh: 他们希望将来能进行大量这样的改造。

sentences.en: They work on all kinds of construction projects, but they don't talk about this building like a regular construction project.
sentences.zh: 他们从事各种建筑项目，但他们谈论这栋楼时，不像是在谈论普通的建筑项目。

sentences.en: They talk about it like a mission.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论它就像是在谈论一项使命。

sentences.en: What we're doing here is, is impactful.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里所做的事情，是有影响力的。

sentences.en: It's huge.
sentences.zh: 意义重大。

sentences.en: That's Joey.
sentences.zh: 那是乔伊。

sentences.en: And doing our part for the overall greater good and the sustainability goals and environmental goals for the city.
sentences.zh: 我们正在为整体的共同利益、城市的可持续发展目标和环境目标尽自己的一份力量。

sentences.en: So in terms of what you have, where we're going, we are now, we're going to a finished unit or something that feels like a solution?
sentences.zh: 那么，就你所拥有的，我们正要去的地方，我们现在是要去一个完工的单元，还是一个感觉像是解决方案的地方？

sentences.en: Yeah, we'll go down to the third floor.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们要去三楼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And we'll go to our finished unit.
sentences.zh: 我们要去我们的完工单元。

sentences.en: In theory, these conversions make a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 理论上，这些改造非常有意义。

sentences.en: But walking around the Water Street construction site, it became obvious to me these projects are more complicated than swapping out one kind of tenant for another.
sentences.zh: 但在沃特街建筑工地走了一圈后，我很明显地感觉到，这些项目比简单地更换租户类型要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And for all those folks who just want to take empty office towers and fill them with condos, they really have their work cut out for them.
sentences.zh: 对于那些只想把空置办公楼填满公寓的人来说，他们确实任重道远。

sentences.en: In How Buildings Learned, Stuart Brand talks about how for a building to be long-lasting, it needs to be flexible.
sentences.zh: 在《建筑如何学习》中，斯图尔特·布兰德谈到，建筑要长久，就需要具备灵活性。

sentences.en: A great example of this are old Victorian townhouses in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 旧金山的维多利亚式联排别墅就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Stuart Brand talks about how these townhouses often find second lives as apartments.
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特·布兰德谈到这些联排别墅如何经常作为公寓获得第二次生命。

sentences.en: On each floor, there are three to six rooms, so the houses are easy to divide into two or three flats, one per floor.
sentences.zh: 每层楼有三到六个房间，所以这些房子很容易分成两到三套公寓，每层一套。

sentences.en: The rooms are modest in size and unspecified in function.
sentences.zh: 房间大小适中，功能不固定。

sentences.en: These houses offer boundless flexibility.
sentences.zh: 这些房子提供了无限的灵活性。

sentences.en: An office building, by contrast, does not have the same boundless flexibility.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，办公楼并不具备同样的无限灵活性。

sentences.en: At the Water Street site, there were all these bare wires and steel beams everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在沃特街工地，到处都是裸露的电线和钢梁。

sentences.en: It looked like they were gutting the building.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们正在把大楼掏空。

sentences.en: It's definitely a massive, massive undertaking.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一项极其艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: New York Times reporter Emily Badger.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》记者艾米丽·巴杰。

sentences.en: You know, if people who are advocating for this are envisioning, you know, we just need to throw up a few more walls and install some new toilets, like,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果那些倡导者设想的是，我们只需要多砌几堵墙，安装几个新马桶，那么，

sentences.en: that is not at all what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是我们所谈论的情况。

sentences.en: Office conversions are a ton of work because most office buildings aren't designed in the same way you design an apartment building.
sentences.zh: 办公楼改建工作量巨大，因为大多数办公楼的设计方式与公寓楼不同。

sentences.en: And that means you have to do a lot of renovation.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你必须进行大量的翻新。

sentences.en: For example, you need to have, like, 50 bathrooms, 50 small bathrooms on a floor where you used to have, like, two very large bathrooMs.
sentences.zh: 例如，你需要在一个以前只有两个超大卫生间的楼层里，安装50个小卫生间。

sentences.en: So, like, you only have bathrooms and plumbing in one location.
sentences.zh: 所以，以前你只有一个地方有卫生间和管道系统。

sentences.en: And now you need to, like, distribute it throughout the rest of the building.
sentences.zh: 而现在你需要将其分配到建筑的其他部分。

sentences.en: To fix this, developers have to redo the plumbing.
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，开发商必须重做管道系统。

sentences.en: And, of course, they also have to reckon with parking.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们还必须考虑停车问题。

sentences.en: Maybe now the municipality says you have to have a certain parking requirement because it's an apartment building.
sentences.zh: 也许现在市政部门说，因为它是公寓楼，所以必须满足一定的停车要求。

sentences.en: And, like, do you have the capacity to put parking garage space in the basement?
sentences.zh: 那么，你有能力在地下室设置停车库空间吗？

sentences.en: So, no.
sentences.zh: 所以，不行。

sentences.en: Sadly, you cannot just throw up walls and call it a day.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，你不能只是砌几堵墙就完事了。

sentences.en: The Water Street development was a clear reflection of how much labor was required for these conversions.
sentences.zh: 沃特街的开发项目清楚地反映了这些改造需要付出多少劳动。

sentences.en: The inside is a new building.
sentences.zh: 内部是一栋全新的建筑。

sentences.en: Everything is brand new.
sentences.zh: 一切都是全新的。

sentences.en: We've replaced everything and we took it down to the structure.
sentences.zh: 我们更换了一切，并将其拆解到了结构层面。

sentences.en: Brand new building on the inside and it'll look brand new on the outside as well.
sentences.zh: 内部是全新的建筑，外观看起来也会是全新的。

sentences.en: I mean, in that case, like, is, I know it's a conversion.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这种情况下，我知道这是一种改造。

sentences.en: I know it's an adaptive reuse, but, like, is it?
sentences.zh: 我知道这是适应性再利用，但真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Like, it sounds like it's a new building.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像是一栋新建筑。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Joey confirmed to me they could reuse the foundation and the concrete floors.
sentences.zh: Joey向我证实，他们可以重复利用地基和混凝土楼板。

sentences.en: And, I mean, that's pretty big.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，这非常重要。

sentences.en: But most everything else is new.
sentences.zh: 但其他大部分东西都是新的。

sentences.en: He did add this project was still cheaper than a totally new building.
sentences.zh: 他确实补充说，这个项目仍然比建造一栋全新的建筑要便宜。

sentences.en: The amount of material that would be required and time to reconstruct the structure itself,
sentences.zh: 重建结构本身所需的材料量和时间，

sentences.en: all of the concrete and the steel, it's really utilizing those same bones that are good bones.
sentences.zh: 所有的混凝土和钢材，实际上是在利用那些良好的骨架。

sentences.en: It's reusing those and just changing everything else.
sentences.zh: 重复利用它们，只改变其他一切。

sentences.en: The developers took me down to a model apartment.
sentences.zh: 开发商带我参观了一个样板间。

sentences.en: And I have to say, it was really nice.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，真的很不错。

sentences.en: Beautiful views, just all new amenities.
sentences.zh: 美丽的景色，所有设施都是全新的。

sentences.en: The only indications it was an old office building were the high ceilings and the very big doors.
sentences.zh: 唯一能看出它是旧办公楼的迹象就是高高的天花板和非常大的门。

sentences.en: We went with eight-foot doors.
sentences.zh: 我们选用了八英尺高的门。

sentences.en: Yeah, those are tall.
sentences.zh: 是的，那很高。

sentences.en: It really makes it much more grand.
sentences.zh: 这确实让空间显得更加宏伟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A lot of typical residential buildings go with seven foot or even seven-six.
sentences.zh: 很多典型的住宅楼会选用七英尺甚至七英尺六英寸的门。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Maybe the biggest complication when you're doing an office-to-apartment conversion is the floor plate.
sentences.zh: 当你进行办公楼改公寓时，最大的困难可能就是楼板。

sentences.en: Architects use the term floor plate to describe the size of the area inside the walls of each story of the building.
sentences.zh: 建筑师用“楼板”这个术语来描述建筑每一层墙内区域的大小。

sentences.en: So, you know, the size of the floor.
sentences.zh: 也就是楼层的面积。

sentences.en: And there was a time when a residential floor plate and one for an office building were basically identical.
sentences.zh: 曾经有一段时间，住宅楼板和办公楼楼板基本是一样的。

sentences.en: It used to be the case, you know, a hundred years ago, that we built office buildings in America that were shaped very similar to apartment buildings.
sentences.zh: 一百年前，我们在美国建造的办公楼形状和公寓楼非常相似。

sentences.en: You know, they were very narrow.
sentences.zh: 它们非常狭窄。

sentences.en: You know, many of them were like rectangular in shape.
sentences.zh: 很多都是长方形的。

sentences.en: At the time, most of these buildings were relatively narrow because all light and ventilation came from windows.
sentences.zh: 当时，大多数建筑都比较狭窄，因为所有的光线和通风都来自窗户。

sentences.en: And every office worker needed to be close to one.
sentences.zh: 每个办公人员都需要靠近窗户。

sentences.en: So these really old office buildings that were sort of built with these same constraints that residential buildings are built with today,
sentences.zh: 所以这些非常古老的办公楼，在建造时受到与今天住宅楼相同的限制，

sentences.en: they make for great conversion prospects because fundamentally the shape of them is similar.
sentences.zh: 它们是非常好的改造对象，因为从根本上讲，它们的形状是相似的。

sentences.en: But post-World War II, offices got some upgrades like air conditioning and fluorescent lighting.
sentences.zh: 但二战后，办公室进行了一些升级，比如空调和荧光灯。

sentences.en: And suddenly office workers didn't need to be sitting next to a window all the time.
sentences.zh: 突然间，办公人员不需要一直坐在窗边了。

sentences.en: So office floor plates got a lot bigger.
sentences.zh: 所以办公楼的楼板变得大多了。

sentences.en: Today, office buildings tend to have much wider, deeper floor plates than apartments,
sentences.zh: 今天，办公楼的楼板往往比公寓更宽、更深，

sentences.en: which means there's a lot of interior space that's pretty far from a window.
sentences.zh: 这意味着有很多内部空间离窗户很远。

sentences.en: And that makes conversions really complicated, unless you want a bunch of apartment units with zero access to natural light.
sentences.zh: 这使得改造变得非常复杂，除非你想要一堆完全没有自然采光的公寓单元。

sentences.en: Many cities, including New York, have a legal requirement that bedrooms have access to operable windows.
sentences.zh: 包括纽约在内的许多城市都有法律要求，卧室必须有可开启的窗户。

sentences.en: Like, you literally have to be able to open it and get fresh air inside.
sentences.zh: 你必须能够打开窗户，让新鲜空气进来。

sentences.en: This means developers working on office-to-apartment conversions are left with a bunch of empty space in the middle of these buildings.
sentences.zh: 这意味着从事办公改公寓的开发商，在这些建筑的中间会留下一大片空置空间。

sentences.en: Some developers just put amenities in there, like gyms or media rooMs.
sentences.zh: 一些开发商只是把那里用作配套设施，比如健身房或媒体室。

sentences.en: So, like, the game room will be located somewhere like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，游戏室之类的设施会设在那种地方。

sentences.en: But, I mean, you don't need, like, 20 floors of game rooms in a modern apartment building.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，现代公寓楼里不需要20层楼的游戏室。

sentences.en: But that's sort of fundamentally at the center of this conversion problem.
sentences.zh: 但这正是这个改造问题的核心所在。

sentences.en: It's like, what do you do with interior space that's just not a nice place to live?
sentences.zh: 就像，你该如何处理那些不适合居住的内部空间呢？

sentences.en: At the Water Street site, Van Barton had a different idea.
sentences.zh: 在Water Street的项目现场，Van Barton有一个不同的想法。

sentences.en: They would take all that interior space and just wall it off.
sentences.zh: 他们打算把所有的内部空间都围起来。

sentences.en: So, what you'll see inside is we cut out a series of three voids.
sentences.zh: 所以，你在里面会看到我们切出了一系列三个空洞。

sentences.en: So, they're basically blind shafts into the floor plate.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上是深入楼板的盲井。

sentences.en: A blind shaft is this void in the center of the building that's inaccessible to tenants.
sentences.zh: 盲井是建筑中心的一个租户无法进入的空洞。

sentences.en: The voids are actually useful for Joey and his company because zoning limits the square footage for an apartment building.
sentences.zh: 这些空洞对Joey和他的公司来说实际上很有用，因为分区规划限制了公寓楼的建筑面积。

sentences.en: But the voids don't count.
sentences.zh: 但这些空洞不计入面积。

sentences.en: So, they can take that unused square footage and just build new floors on top.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们可以利用那些未使用的面积，在顶部加盖新楼层。

sentences.en: If we deduct it here, we could then reallocate it elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 如果我们在这里扣除它，就可以把它重新分配到其他地方。

sentences.en: So, we took this kind of unusable, very much less valuable space at the back end of a unit from there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们从单元后部那种不可用、价值较低的空间里腾出了面积。

sentences.en: And took it and put it up at the top of the building where it's much more valuable.
sentences.zh: 并把它用到了建筑顶部，那里更有价值。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Some builders are willing to put in the effort and do something with this unusable middle space and adapt the building for reuse.
sentences.zh: 一些建筑商愿意投入精力，利用这些不可用的中间空间，并对建筑进行改造再利用。

sentences.en: I mean, come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: What's a few voids between friends?
sentences.zh: 朋友之间几个空洞算什么？

sentences.en: Even if a builder makes it this far, they're going to find a whole new set of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 即使建筑商走到了这一步，他们也会发现一堆全新的问题。

sentences.en: And that's a big old pile of red tape.
sentences.zh: 那是一大堆繁文缛节。

sentences.en: Converting a building from an office to an apartment, because it's a use change, sort of triggers your need to now comply with, like,
sentences.zh: 将建筑从办公楼改为公寓，因为用途发生了改变，这会触发你遵守，比如，

sentences.en: a totally different regulatory regime than the one under which the building was built.
sentences.zh: 一套与建筑建造时完全不同的监管制度。

sentences.en: It kind of goes without saying.
sentences.zh: 这不言而喻。

sentences.en: But office buildings follow a different set of rules than housing.
sentences.zh: 但办公楼遵循的规则与住宅不同。

sentences.en: You know, we just have all of these rules that govern the built environment in cities.
sentences.zh: 我们有各种各样的规则来管理城市中的建筑环境。

sentences.en: And, you know, those rules often don't envision converting offices into housing.
sentences.zh: 而这些规则往往没有预见到将办公室改造成住宅的情况。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it turns out to be incredibly difficult to convert from one use to another and do it in a legal manner.
sentences.zh: 所以，事实证明，以合法的方式将一种用途转换为另一种用途是非常困难的。

sentences.en: There are many bylaws and rules that keep people alive, like fire codes.
sentences.zh: 有很多章程和规则是为了保障人们的生命安全，比如消防法规。

sentences.en: We like those.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢这些。

sentences.en: But New York has a very particular hurdle that's preventing conversions.
sentences.zh: 但纽约有一个非常特殊的障碍阻碍了改造。

sentences.en: In big parts of the city, commercial buildings constructed after a certain year are not eligible to be fully converted into housing.
sentences.zh: 在城市的大部分地区，在某一年之后建造的商业建筑没有资格被完全改造成住宅。

sentences.en: Here's Dan Garotnik.
sentences.zh: 这是Dan Garotnik。

sentences.en: In New York City, for most buildings, that date is 1961.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市，对于大多数建筑来说，这个日期是1961年。

sentences.en: If you were built before 1961 and you're in a zone which allows for residential, you can convert.
sentences.zh: 如果你是在1961年之前建造的，并且位于允许住宅用途的区域，你就可以进行改造。

sentences.en: And if you're not, you're out of luck.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，那你就没戏了。

sentences.en: This rule is known as the cutoff year.
sentences.zh: 这条规则被称为“截止年份”。

sentences.en: And the cutoff year is in place because, I mean, I, you know, somebody must have had some good reason at some point.
sentences.zh: 这个截止年份之所以存在，是因为，有人在某个时候一定有充分的理由。

sentences.en: When I first read about this, I did not really understand why New York has this rule.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次读到这个规定时，我真的不明白为什么纽约会有这条规则。

sentences.en: And to be honest, I still don't.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我现在也不明白。

sentences.en: This is an argument that was given to me by someone which I don't find very convincing.
sentences.zh: 这是某人给我的一个论点，我觉得不太有说服力。

sentences.en: So it's not going to be very convincing to you either.
sentences.zh: 所以对你来说也不会很有说服力。

sentences.en: But we don't want developers sort of building things where they're telling us it's an office building,
sentences.zh: 但我们不希望开发商建造一些东西，他们告诉我们那是办公楼，

sentences.en: but they're really planning for it to be a residential building in five years.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他们计划五年后将其变成住宅楼。

sentences.en: And I actually am not sure what the problem with that is.
sentences.zh: 我其实不确定这有什么问题。

sentences.en: There are neighborhoods in New York that have exceptions, like the financial district,
sentences.zh: 纽约有一些社区有例外，比如金融区，

sentences.en: where the conversion deadline is 1977 instead of 1961.
sentences.zh: 那里的改造截止日期是1977年，而不是1961年。

sentences.en: But in most of the city, conversions are just really hard.
sentences.zh: 但在城市的大部分地区，改造真的很难。

sentences.en: Joey Shaleli told me these rules make it very, very difficult to even find candidates for these conversions.
sentences.zh: Joey Shaleli告诉我，这些规则使得寻找改造候选建筑变得非常非常困难。

sentences.en: There's a lot of product that was built after 77 and definitely after 61 that is now in this kind of gray space.
sentences.zh: 有很多77年之后，尤其是61年之后建造的产品，现在处于这种灰色地带。

sentences.en: A lot of 1980s builds.
sentences.zh: 很多80年代的建筑。

sentences.en: We owned a building right across the street, 175 water.
sentences.zh: 我们在街对面拥有一栋建筑，175 Water。

sentences.en: That other building was built after 1977, which is the cutoff year in this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 那栋建筑建于1977年之后，也就是该社区的截止年份。

sentences.en: So the conversion didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 所以改造没有发生。

sentences.en: The cutoff year is this confusing piece of bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 截止年份是一个令人困惑的官僚主义产物。

sentences.en: But in August, the city announced a plan to change this rule to move up the cutoff year
sentences.zh: 但在八月，市政府宣布了一项改变这一规则的计划，以推迟截止年份，

sentences.en: in the hopes it would spur more conversions, especially in midtown Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 希望这能刺激更多的改造，特别是在曼哈顿中城。

sentences.en: While New York developers are waiting for changes to the cutoff year's rule,
sentences.zh: 当纽约的开发商等待截止年份规则的改变时，

sentences.en: there are other rules about apartments that no one wants to do away with.
sentences.zh: 还有其他关于公寓的规则是没人想废除的。

sentences.en: In fact, most of the red tape around apartments comes from the era of dangerous tenement buildings in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 事实上，围绕公寓的大部分繁文缛节都源于19世纪危险的廉租房时代。

sentences.en: In big cities like New York, new immigrants would move into unsanitary apartments without access to sunlight and fresh air and toilets.
sentences.zh: 在纽约这样的大城市，新移民会搬进不卫生的公寓，没有阳光、新鲜空气和厕所。

sentences.en: New laws were adopted in the early 20th century to protect poor renters.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初通过了新法律来保护贫困租户。

sentences.en: Again, we like these regulations.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们喜欢这些法规。

sentences.en: In many ways, New York is a special case.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，纽约是一个特例。

sentences.en: Like, other cities just do not have this weird cutoff year thing.
sentences.zh: 其他城市并没有这种奇怪的截止年份限制。

sentences.en: But every city has its own set of issues and its own set of onerous rules when it comes to converting offices into apartments.
sentences.zh: 但每个城市在将办公室改造成公寓时，都有自己的一套问题和繁重的规则。

sentences.en: In many communities in California, the seismic requirements that you are expected to meet for an apartment building
sentences.zh: 在加州的许多社区，你被要求满足的公寓楼抗震要求，

sentences.en: are different and more stringent than they are for an office.
sentences.zh: 与办公楼不同，而且更严格。

sentences.en: And so, if you want to successfully convert a building, you literally have to, you know, reinforce the entire structure of the building
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想成功改造一栋建筑，你必须，加固建筑的整个结构，

sentences.en: to make it, you know, more structurally sound in the event of an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 使其在地震发生时结构更稳固。

sentences.en: Or, you know, in places in the South where there's a lot of concerns about hurricanes,
sentences.zh: 或者，在南方那些非常担心飓风的地方，

sentences.en: now you need to comply with the wind load ratings that we expect of buildings in 2023,
sentences.zh: 现在你需要遵守我们2023年对建筑要求的风荷载等级，

sentences.en: not in 1960 when that building was built.
sentences.zh: 而不是1960年建筑建造时的标准。

sentences.en: And now you have to, you know, completely redo the glazing and everything on the building.
sentences.zh: 现在你必须完全重做建筑的玻璃幕墙和一切设施。

sentences.en: Like, that's adding an enormous amount of expense.
sentences.zh: 这增加了巨大的开支。

sentences.en: I noticed something else about office conversions walking around the Water Street construction site.
sentences.zh: 在Water Street施工现场走动时，我注意到了关于办公楼改造的另一件事。

sentences.en: It was while Joey was excitedly telling me about all of the amenities he was planning for this building.
sentences.zh: 当时Joey正兴奋地向我介绍他为这栋楼规划的所有配套设施。

sentences.en: We're going to have a two-lane bowling alley, a sportsbook room with a giant 12-foot by 8-foot TV.
sentences.zh: 我们将拥有一个双球道保龄球馆，一个带有12英尺乘8英尺巨型电视的体育博彩室。

sentences.en: And then we'll have a very expansive gym with techno gym equipment.
sentences.zh: 然后我们将拥有一个配备泰诺健设备的宽敞健身房。

sentences.en: We'll have a spa and hot tub with a cold plunge and treatment rooMs.
sentences.zh: 我们将拥有一个带冷水池和理疗室的水疗中心和热水浴缸。

sentences.en: The amenities sounded great.
sentences.zh: 这些设施听起来很棒。

sentences.en: But the more I heard about them, the more it sounded like this apartment building might be a little out of my price range.
sentences.zh: 但我听到的越多，就越觉得这栋公寓楼可能超出了我的预算。

sentences.en: I wonder, like, when this is open, what's it going to rent for?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，当它开放时，租金会是多少？

sentences.en: Like, what are the units going to be?
sentences.zh: 单元会是什么样的？

sentences.en: So anywhere, you know, it really ranges.
sentences.zh: 范围很广。

sentences.en: I'd say anywhere from maybe $3,500 to $4,000 on a studio to $4,500 to $5,500 or up to $6,000 on a one-bed.
sentences.zh: 我想单间公寓可能在3500到4000美元，一居室在4500到5500甚至6000美元。

sentences.en: And then a two-bed anywhere from, call it $6,500 or $7,000 on up.
sentences.zh: 两居室的话，起价在6500或7000美元左右。

sentences.en: With all of the expense of making a conversion like this, the units are going to be available at the market rate, which in New York is quite expensive.
sentences.zh: 由于这种改造的费用很高，这些单元将以市场价格提供，这在纽约相当昂贵。

sentences.en: In Manhattan right now, the average apartment is over $4,500.
sentences.zh: 目前在曼哈顿，平均公寓租金超过4500美元。

sentences.en: I'm sure there's going to be a lot of competition to live here.

sentences.en: So it's not a one size fits all.

sentences.en: There's an argument that every new unit of housing is important.

sentences.en: But so far, that idea hasn't gained much traction.

sentences.en: This is just sitting here empty.

sentences.en: Including Dan Garodnik from the city of New York.

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean it's not worth pursuing.
